- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., < -0.30) and price is trending down, model often undercorrects; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply 2–4% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until reversion.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.40 to -0.30) triggers model lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., -0.30+ for 3+ days), model underestimates true price; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast.
